extracted.intended_audience: researchers (academic and industry) submitting systems papers to OSDI '25
extracted.subtask_description: Call-for-papers and submission/review rules for the 19th USENIX Symposium on Operating Systems Design and Implementation (OSDI '25), describing what makes a good paper, formatting/anonymity/conflict requirements, and review/author-response procedures. Intended to guide authors in preparing and submitting conference papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will be judged on novelty, significance, interest, clarity, relevance, and correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted papers will be shepherded through editorial review by a program committee member. Reviewers evaluate these aspects when deciding on acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivate a significant problem
rubrics_metrics.description: A good paper will motivate a significant problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explain why the problem matters to computer systems research and/or practice and why it deserves attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose an interesting and compelling solution
rubrics_metrics.description: A good paper will propose an interesting and compelling solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed approach should be novel, well-motivated, and presented clearly enough for reviewers to judge its merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate practicality and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: A good paper will demonstrate the practicality and benefits of the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative or qualitative evidence (measurements, evaluations, case studies) that the solution works and yields benefits; practicality should be clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw appropriate conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A good paper will draw appropriate conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should follow from the presented results without overclaiming; discuss limitations and scope where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly describe contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: A good paper will clearly describe the paper's contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the contributions explicitly and make it easy for reviewers to identify what is new and valuable in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate advances beyond previous work
rubrics_metrics.description: A good paper will clearly articulate the advances beyond previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare to related work and explain how the submission advances the state of the art or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic relevance to computer systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will evaluate submissions based on topic relevance to computer systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSDI takes a broad view of systems but prioritizes work that clearly fits within operating systems, storage, distributed systems, cloud, security/reliability of systems, systems aspects of big data, embedded systems, virtualization, networking related to OS, management/troubleshooting, and interfaces to architecture/languages/databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to impact future research and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider the submission's potential to impact future research and practices in computer systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should demonstrate how their contributions could influence subsequent research, system designs, or real-world practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to a substantial portion of OSDI attendees
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must demonstrate relevance and offer unique insights to capture the interest of a substantial portion of OSDI attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because OSDI is single-track, selected papers should foster deep discussions and be broadly interesting to the community attending the symposium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and length requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted papers must be no longer than 12 single-spaced 8.5" x 11" pages (including figures and tables), using 10-point type on 12-point leading, two-column format, Times Roman or similar, within a text block 7" x 9". References may occupy additional pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pages should be numbered; figures and tables should be legible in black and white without magnification. Papers not meeting these criteria will be rejected without review. Templates are available; no deadline extensions for reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers will be allowed 14 pages in the proceedings, plus references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare final versions within the proceedings limits if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended abstracts discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers so short as to be considered 'extended abstracts' will not receive full consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submission contains sufficient technical substance for full review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may upload supplementary material separate from submissions; PC members are not required to read supplementary material, so each paper should stand alone without it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use supplementary files for peripheral but useful material (sketched formal proofs, code snippets, extra methodological detail). Do not rely on supplementary material to convince the PC of core claims. Attaching supplementary material is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity blinding (double-blind review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is double-blind. Authors must make a good-faith effort to anonymize submissions and must not identify themselves or their institutions explicitly or by implication (e.g., through references or acknowledgments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions violating formatting and anonymization rules will be rejected without review. If uncertain about anonymization, contact program co-chairs well in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must register abstracts prior to full paper submission; abstract registration is essential for PC members to identify qualified reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts lacking sufficient information (empty, placeholder, or trivial abstracts) will be rejected, which will preclude paper submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest disclosure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When registering abstracts, authors must provide conflicts with PC members. A conflict exists if: (a) same current institution or employed there within past two years (excluding concluded internships), or will begin employment during review; (b) past or present thesis advisor/advisee relationship; (c) collaboration on a project/publication/grant/program co-chairship/editorship within past two years; (d) close family relatives (spouse, domestic partner, parents, children).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not list conflicts if none of these circumstances applies. Examples not sufficient to claim conflict include previous review of the work, being employed by a competitor, being a friend, being a post-doc advisor/advisee, or having the same advisor. Chairs will review conflicts and may add/remove them or reject abstracts/papers for missing/extraneous conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submission and plagiarism prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submission to multiple venues, submission of previously published work, or plagiarism constitutes dishonesty or fraud and is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USENIX may take action against authors who commit these practices; see USENIX Conference Submissions Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously submitted-to-other-conference policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a paper that had been previously submitted to and not accepted by another conference is permitted if authors have substantially addressed previous reviewers' comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior conference's rejection notification was received less than thirteen months before the OSDI deadline, authors are requested to provide information about the previous submission and a summary of revisions. Upload this via the submission form; it will not be shared with OSDI reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior/concurrent workshop publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior or concurrent workshop publication does not preclude publishing a related paper in OSDI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission form will require a copy of the related workshop paper and a short explanation of new material in the conference paper beyond the workshop version. Co-chairs may share the workshop paper with the workshop's organizers and discuss it with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior/concurrent non-peer-reviewed publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior or concurrent publication in non-peer-reviewed contexts (arXiv, technical reports, talks, social-media posts) is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OSDI submission must use an anonymized name for your project or system that differs from any used in such contexts to preserve double-blind review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondisclosure agreements not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers accompanied by nondisclosure agreement (NDA) forms will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attach NDA forms to submissions; such papers will be excluded from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and system
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be in PDF format and submitted via the conference submission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the detailed submission requirements and use provided templates for LaTeX/Word. Follow file-format rules to avoid desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author attendance and presentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting, authors agree that at least one author will attend the conference to present the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration fees pose hardship or special circumstances (travel restrictions, health), contact USENIX; remote presentation and Q&A may be possible in very special cases. For visa invitation letters, contact USENIX early and identify yourself as a presenter/author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response period constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: During the author-response period, responses must be limited to (a) correcting factual errors in reviews or (b) directly addressing questions posed by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must not include new experiments/data, describe additional work completed since submission, or promise additional work. Submission of a response is optional; responses may be any length up to 2000 words, but a shorter, crisper response is often advantageous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise-and-resubmit option
rubrics_metrics.description: Some rejected papers may be offered an option to revise and resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offered, authors will receive a list of issues to address and may resubmit a revised version with a response to those issues; if accepted after resubmission, the paper will be presented at OSDI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions will be treated as confidential prior to publication on the OSDI '25 website; rejected submissions will be permanently treated as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted papers will be available online to registered attendees before the conference unless authors notify the provided email that they prefer otherwise; papers become available publicly on the first day of the symposium.
